answer:
For a new series added to an existing registered open-end fund trust, a Rule 485(a) post-effective amendment ordinarily becomes effective **60 days after filing**, unless the SEC accelerates or the filing specifies a later date. That is the statutory default for a substantive amendment under Securities Act Rule 485(a), not a promise that the ETF can launch on that date.

It is only the registration-statement effectiveness period. Launch may still depend on completing other work—such as exchange listing approval, operational and distribution readiness, and any required regulatory steps—and the SEC may review the filing or the effective date may be delayed. “No separate exemptive relief” removes one potential dependency, not all launch conditions.

This differs from **initial registration of a new trust**: an initial Form N-1A is generally subject to the **75-day** effectiveness period under Securities Act Section 8(a), absent acceleration or another applicable provision.
